title: Drawback Chess, But I Don't Know My Drawback
summary: Drawback Chess on the Drawback Chess site, except the creator's own drawback is hidden from him (shown as dashes) and the opponent's is hidden too. Goal: win one game. Game 1 (White) he instantly loses on move 2 to 'Two Steps Forward One Step Back'. Game 2 loses to 'Eye for an Eye'. Game 3 (Black) wins with hidden drawback 'True Love' (opponent had 'Body Snatcher'). Game 4 (White) wins with hidden 'King of the Hill' (four highlighted mystery squares in the centre) vs opponent's 'Nurturer'.
rules: Standard chess setup and movement, 5-minute (+5) clocks, kings can be captured (Drawback Chess has no check rule; you win by taking the king).
Each player is assigned a random drawback from a large pool (hundreds). Violating it, or having no legal move that obeys it, loses the game immediately ('You lost due to your drawback').
In this mode the player's own drawback is HIDDEN (header shows 'Drawbacks: ---'); illegal moves under the drawback are simply unavailable, which is the only hint.

Drawbacks seen in the video: Two Steps Forward One Step Back (if you move forward two times in a row you must move backwards next); Eye for an Eye (if your opponent captures, you must capture on your next move or lose); True Love; King of the Hill (four mystery squares in the middle of the board are highlighted as a hint); opponent drawbacks Rook Fan Club (must promote to rooks), Ivory Tower, Body Snatcher, Nurturer.
The drawback is revealed after the game (match history / result screen).
win_condition: Capture/checkmate the enemy king without (unknowingly) breaking your hidden drawback; goal of the video was to win one game.
